open_findings.title: BESS sizing constants are a factor-of-10 trap
open_findings.detail: Active backend is _SimpleBESSModel (PYSAM_ACTIVE=False): E_NOM_MWH=15.0, P_MAX_MW=5.0. The bess.py module docstring and _PySAMBESSModel advertise 150 MWh / 50 MW. Logged soc_final / bess_soc is a FRACTION, not MWh.
open_findings.impact: nominal stored MWh computed with 150.0 would be 10x wrong, and the SOC term already dominates the day's regulation revenue.
open_findings.fix: nominal_stored_MWh = soc_fraction * env._fast_env._bess.E_NOM_MWH read at runtime from the instantiated model; assert E_NOM_MWH == 15.0 and P_MAX_MW == 5.0 in the driver preamble.

open_findings.title: Grid-relief energy must use NET BESS, not discharge alone
open_findings.detail: integral(P_ref - P_grid) = facility_relief_mwh + (bess_discharge_mwh - bess_charge_mwh). Existing CSV schema carries both columns.
open_findings.impact: using discharge alone overstates grid relief by the full charge energy.

open_findings.title: Three stale-definition traps in cooling and sign conventions
detail: ThermalTwin.p_cool_nominal_mw returns 36.5 MW (pump at PUMP_NOM_SPEED=1.0) but the actual reference applies float32(0.7) to BOTH hvac and pump, drawing ~36.05 MW. In physical_v1 the p_cool_nominal_mw path is dead code; do not describe the reference as 'pump at nominal 1.0'.

cool_delta_kw has two definitions: physical mode = p_cooling - p_cooling_ref (INCLUDES the Zone-A chiller); legacy mode = p_hvac + p_pump - p_cool_nominal (EXCLUDES it). Use only the physical value and label it as chiller-inclusive.

macro_grid.step() docstring says delta_p_kw positive = 'increase consumption'; env_low_level uses the opposite convention (positive RegD = reduce draw). The field is unused by the env, so this is a doc bug only - do not inherit the sign from the docstring.
open_findings.impact: mislabeled cooling baseline or inverted sign in the narrative.
open_findings.fix: take all cooling components from logged nominal-trajectory diagnostics; state the physical-mode definitions in the report.

caveats_required_in_report.text: Cash flow is Delta(regulation revenue) - Delta(grid-import energy cost) BEFORE recovery, degradation and service valuation. It is NOT profit. Measured scale on day 196: regulation revenue 5.62 USD per 15-min macro step vs electricity cost 1921.69 USD per macro step (~540 USD/day vs ~184k USD/day), so the metric is dominated by the energy term, not by regulation.

The cash-flow number is not comparable across candidates with differing terminal SOC. All candidates start at SOC 0.50 (7.5 MWh nominal); a candidate ending at SOC_MIN 0.10 has liquidated 6.0 MWh it never purchased in-episode, which at the day's LMP band exceeds the entire day's regulation revenue by one to two orders of magnitude. Place Delta(nominal stored MWh) = (soc_final - 0.50) * 15.0 adjacent to the cash figure, not in a footnote. No recharge price need be invented: the model itself defines eta_charge = max(0.70, 0.97 - 0.008*C_rate^2 - 0.010*(SOC-0.5)^2) with C_rate = |P|/15, so restoring X MWh of SOC requires X/eta_charge of grid import (~3-4% overhead at low C-rate). That is model-derived, not assumed.

perf_score / mean_paid_perf_score are NOT comparable across candidates. The denominator is max(committed_mw*1000, 100 kW) - the agent's own commitment. Measured: macro floor is 100 kW, so the floor binds only below 0.1 MW and every run sits in the linear regime. A rejected bid (committed = dr_baseline 5 MW) and an accepted 30 MW bid divide the same physical error by 5000 vs 30000 kW. Use absolute mean_tracking_err in kW for cross-candidate tracking comparison; keep perf_score only inside the gross - tracking_discount identity for a single trajectory.

When decomposing Delta(revenue) between a high-macro and rule-macro arm on the same hardware, separate the rate change from the quantity change: rate is the cleared RMCP when the bid is accepted and the fixed dr_rate_usd_mw = 5.0 USD/MW-h when rejected. Report bid_acceptance_fraction alongside. Because marginal revenue per MW committed is exactly rate*hours (V6), the quantity term can move without any change in delivered relief.

Benchmark market payouts are a price/quantity/performance proxy and are not real ISO economics: no capability/mileage split, no two-settlement energy, probabilistic sigmoid clearing. State this once; do not equate to ISO revenue.

Terminal temperature deltas, terminal backlog and terminal SOC are real unpriced end-state differences between candidates. Relief MWh is therefore not a net-energy claim. Report the four end-state terms as raw quantities at their own boundaries; do not form a single 'net relief' scalar by subtracting across boundaries (see W3).

Zone A operated 16.00-29.46 MW against a 16.0 MW idle floor on day 196, so Zone-A throttle headroom is ~13.5 MW and relief from that lever saturates. Facility power ranged 128.5-141.8 MW with cooling at ~36 MW nominal, i.e. these days are cooling-dominated. Useful context for reading component relief; not a defect.

Even at bias 0, RegD has non-zero mean (measured 0.0723 over the sampled window) because the energy-neutrality correction in _step_regd is windowed and the bias term is applied after it with a +/-1 clip. Report regd_clipping_fraction per cell; if non-trivial at bias 0.5 the bias is no longer a clean additive shift.

bess _age_frac resets to 0 on every reset() and reaches 1.0 only at 15,000 MWh throughput. It is a soft RL penalty, not calibrated SoH. Report Delta(age_frac) as a raw diagnostic; do not attach a dollar value or extrapolate lifetime.

per trajectory: agent_ticks == 17280 and terminated == False

summary: With the parent's four corrections applied, no blocking accounting issues remain. All five intended identities (P_fac, P_grid, grid_relief = facility_relief + dBESS, settlement linearity, queue balance) verified exact, and the nominal-as-counterfactual property (V4+V5) is confirmed exact and path-independent, which validates the B_actual - A_actual decomposition design. Three non-blocking findings (F1-F3) and nine required caveats (C1-C9) remain; assertion A3 is the single highest-value free check to run first.
